# Quotable claims

**Generated by `python -m ml.claims`. Do not edit by hand.**

Every number below is resolved from a metrics file at generation time and
carries the exact key path it came from. `ml/test_claims.py` re-resolves all
of them and fails if any has drifted, so a stale number here is a failing
test rather than a wrong slide.

This file exists because four errors in one session were all the same error:
a number copied by hand. One brief swapped the scopes on the headline PR-AUC
pair; `docs/post_submission.md` carried a pair that exists in no metrics file;
an overlap figure was quoted without the qualifier that made it meaningful;
and `ml/early.py` could not run, so the committed metrics were not produced by
the committed source.

**Read the qualifier.** Several of these numbers are wrong if quoted bare --
in particular the coverage shares (unconditional) and the lead-time median
(conditional). The qualifier is part of the claim, not a footnote.

## Sources

- `early_detection` -> `ml/experiments/early_detection/metrics.json`
- `lead_time` -> `ml/experiments/lead_time/metrics.json`
- `ablation` -> `ml/experiments/ablation/results_ablation.json`
- `ibm_aml` -> `ml/experiments/ibm_aml/results_grouped.json`
- `gnn_xgb` -> `ml/experiments/gnn_xgb/results_gnn_xgb.json`
- `stage2` -> `ml/experiments/stage2/metrics.json`

Paths select list elements by field value (`horizons[cutoff_minutes=5]`),
never by position: three horizons were inserted mid-list this session, and
every positional path would now point at a different measurement.

- **0.0085** (span_gradient_span1): mean over 3 seeds; negatives held constant across strata, so compare spans on ROC-AUC or recall@FPR, not on raw PR-AUC
- **0.1740** (span_gradient_span2): mean over 3 seeds; negatives held constant across strata, so compare spans on ROC-AUC or recall@FPR, not on raw PR-AUC
- **0.3279** (span_gradient_span3): mean over 3 seeds; negatives held constant across strata, so compare spans on ROC-AUC or recall@FPR, not on raw PR-AUC
- **0.6220** (pr_auc_t5_cross_bank): mean over 3 seeds, grouped 5-fold CV over rings, 712 pass-through mules
- **0.4282** (pr_auc_t5_single_bank): mean over 3 seeds, grouped 5-fold CV over rings, 712 pass-through mules
- **1.0000** (ring_recall_t180_cross_bank): mean over 3 seeds; ring counts as flagged if any of its mules/collectors is
- **0.9250** (ring_recall_t180_single_bank): mean over 3 seeds; ring counts as flagged if any of its mules/collectors is
- **1.97** (alert_burden_t5_cross_bank): mean over 3 seeds; lower is better
- **6.23** (alert_burden_t5_single_bank): mean over 3 seeds; lower is better
- **0.926** (coverage_span1_cross_bank): UNCONDITIONAL: denominator is every ring of that span, not only the ones that flagged; mean over 3 seeds
- **1.000** (coverage_span2_cross_bank): UNCONDITIONAL: denominator is every ring of that span, not only the ones that flagged; mean over 3 seeds
- **0.944** (coverage_span3_cross_bank): UNCONDITIONAL: denominator is every ring of that span, not only the ones that flagged; mean over 3 seeds
- **0.935** (coverage_span1_single_bank): UNCONDITIONAL: denominator is every ring of that span, not only the ones that flagged; mean over 3 seeds
- **0.826** (coverage_span2_single_bank): UNCONDITIONAL: denominator is every ring of that span, not only the ones that flagged; mean over 3 seeds
- **0.787** (coverage_span3_single_bank): UNCONDITIONAL: denominator is every ring of that span, not only the ones that flagged; mean over 3 seeds
- **0.0** (lead_median_minutes): CONDITIONAL on both scopes flagging inside the grid; zero means cross-bank is not faster. The cross-bank advantage is coverage, not speed -- see lead_rings_tied and coverage_span*
- **90.0** (lead_rings_tied): out of lead_rings_compared rings where both flagged in the grid
- **112.3** (lead_rings_compared): of 120 rings; the remainder are single-bank coverage failures
- **7.7** (lead_only_cross_bank): single-bank reaches these only at the full window, days after the money left; the mirror count is zero
- **3.5** (exit_minutes_p0): property of the generated data, identical across seeds and scopes
- **62.9** (exit_minutes_p25): property of the generated data, identical across seeds and scopes
- **89.4** (exit_minutes_p50): property of the generated data, identical across seeds and scopes
- **113.5** (exit_minutes_p75): property of the generated data, identical across seeds and scopes
- **165.5** (exit_minutes_p100): property of the generated data, identical across seeds and scopes
- **120** (exits_inside_grid): of 120; at the old grid end of T=60m this was 27, which is why share_caught_before_exit was retired
- **0.2448** (ablation_t5_drop_all_identity): mean over 3 seeds, grouped 5-fold CV, same XGBoost recipe as shipped Model A; synthetic data from our own generator -- not a benchmark against real identity-reuse rates; see ml/experiments/ablation/README.md
- **0.9751** (ablation_t180_drop_all_identity): mean over 3 seeds; by T=180m the gap from the T=5m figure above mostly closes -- see ml/experiments/ablation/README.md
- **0.4708** (ablation_t5_identity_only): mean over 3 seeds; higher than the 12-feature transfer-only figure above -- identity reuse is the dominant T=5m signal in this recipe, not a minor supplement; synthetic data, see ml/experiments/ablation/README.md
- **0.0708** (ablation_t5_drop_all_identity_and_age): mean over 3 seeds; the 12-feature transfer-only figure above is itself mostly propped up by this one non-transfer-derived feature -- see ml/experiments/ablation/README.md
- **0.0813** (ibm_aml_xgboost_pr_auc): mean over 3 seeds, grouped CV by connected component; IBM's own synthetic data (CDLA-Sharing-1.0 licence, computational use/Results only -- no IBM data or account-level labels in this repo), base rate 1.23% of accounts positive; NOT comparable to this dataset's published GNN benchmarks (different features, split, and task framing) and not part of this project's own claims -- see ml/experiments/ibm_aml/README.md
- **0.7189** (ibm_aml_giant_component_realized_fpr): 72% of all 515,088 accounts sit in one connected component, so component membership alone is nearly uninformative at this scale; see ml/experiments/ibm_aml/README.md's giant-component finding
- **0.6654** (gnn_xgb_t5_score_averaging): mean over 3 seeds; synthetic simulator data, 30,000 accounts/3 banks; simplest score-averaging combination, not a shipped detector; GNN input includes identity features; gain is +0.044 absolute (~7% relative) -- see ml/experiments/gnn_xgb/README.md
- **0.1398** (gnn_xgb_t5_transfer_only_graph_lift): mean over 3 seeds; synthetic simulator data; shows graph structure carries signal beyond this tree-based feature set, not that this specific gain transfers to real-world data; absolute PR-AUC remains low (0.14) -- see ml/experiments/gnn_xgb/README.md
- **0.8778** (stage1_passthrough_account_recall): account-level; see stage1_ring_recall_count for why this does not carry over to rings 1:1
- **53** (stage1_ring_recall_count): of 120 true rings (44.2%); lower than the 87.8% account recall above because the clustering step drops flagged singletons -- see ml/stage2.py

## Retired claims

### `share_caught_before_exit` -- Share of rings flagged at 1% FPR before the money reached the exit account

It measures the horizon grid, not the detector. A ring can only count if the horizon precedes its cash-out, so the metric is bounded by how many exits have not happened yet. At T=5m only one of 120 rings has cashed out, so the qualifier does nothing and the value collapses onto ring_recall -- identically, to four decimals, for cross-bank. At T=180m every exit has happened, so the metric is structurally 0.0000 even though cross-bank recall is 1.0000 and cross-bank PR-AUC peaks there. It therefore rewards measuring early and punishes measuring well. Replaced by the lead-time claims above, which carry a signed number of minutes and keep unflagged rings out of the average instead of scoring them as on-time.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `0.8694` | share_caught_before_exit at T=5m, cross-bank | `horizons[cutoff_minutes=5].ring_catch.cross_bank.share_caught_before_exit` |
| `0.8694` | ring_recall at T=5m, cross-bank -- identical to the line above | `horizons[cutoff_minutes=5].ring_catch.cross_bank.ring_recall` |
| `0.0000` | share_caught_before_exit at T=180m, cross-bank | `horizons[cutoff_minutes=180].ring_catch.cross_bank.share_caught_before_exit` |
| `1.0000` | ring_recall at T=180m, cross-bank -- while the share above is zero | `horizons[cutoff_minutes=180].ring_catch.cross_bank.ring_recall` |
| `119.0` | Rings whose money had not yet reached the exit at T=5m | `horizons[cutoff_minutes=5].ring_catch.cross_bank.rings_money_not_yet_at_exit` |
| `0.0` | Rings whose money had not yet reached the exit at T=180m | `horizons[cutoff_minutes=180].ring_catch.cross_bank.rings_money_not_yet_at_exit` |

## Slow-drip stress test (appended section)

Sourced from `ml/experiments/slow_drip/metrics.json`; generated, do not edit by hand.
Question: do the rule, an unsupervised Isolation Forest and XGBoost still catch
rings whose hops are slower than the velocity rule's ceiling and whose amounts
are small? The overlay is a separate synthetic world; `simulator/out` is untouched.

**Ring caught** = at least one pass-through member (mule/collector) alerted.
**False alert** = alerted account, whose role is not mule/collector/source.
**Thresholds**: score-based detectors: top 1% of each bank's accounts (ceil) chosen without labels; second budget = per-bank alert count of the velocity rule in the same world; rule uses its fixed shipped constants.
The velocity rule is not given a budget; it alerts wherever its fixed conditions hold,
so its alert count differs from the 300 alerts (1% per bank)
the score-based detectors get; the `alerts raised` rows show both.
Read the negative results in the table as plainly as the positive ones.
